children: While PLS Group was expected to proceed with the P2000 lithium project, Jefferies notes a final investment decision was accelerated relative to prior company commentary. There weren't many shocks in PLS's announcement. Capex of A$1.9 billion and a timeline for maiden production of the September quarter of 2029 were largely in line with Jefferies's expectations. "PLS continues to demonstrate its countercyclical investment strategy with a development approach centred on being in the market to reap outsize benefit from price fly-up scenarios," analyst Mitch Ryan says. Jefferies retains a buy call, but trims its price target on PLS by 9.1% to A$5.00/share. PLS ended last week at A$2.98. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
